perf.summary: A fresh 'next' buffer is stackalloc'd inside the per-k loop, growing stack usage and re-zeroing every iteration; it can be a single reused buffer (the 'tmp' parameter exists for exactly this but is unused).
perf.currentCost: stackalloc long[n] executed up to n times within the k-loop (n*n longs of stack pressure / repeated frame growth) plus an n-length zero pass each iteration, and a separate n-length copy 'gpow[j]=next[j]' each iteration.
perf.proposedChange: Allocate 'next' once (or use the unused 'tmp' parameter) outside the loop. Better: ping-pong between gpow and next pointers (swap the two pointers) to eliminate the per-iteration 'gpow[j]=next[j]' copy entirely; just zero the target buffer before the convolution.
perf.rationale: stackalloc inside a loop is a known anti-pattern (frame does not shrink until method exit in C#, so it accumulates), and pointer ping-pong removes an O(n) copy pass per k, cutting an O(n^2) copy cost to zero. The 'tmp' parameter is currently dead, indicating intended scratch reuse.
perf.risk: Must still zero the destination buffer before each convolution accumulation (it does 'next[j]=0'). Ping-pong requires care that the final gpow read after the loop points at the right buffer, but gpow is not read after the loop here. Safe and behavior-preserving.

perf.summary: RunNaive is a byte-for-byte duplicate of Run (minus the unused tmp parameter), doubling code/icache footprint with no behavioral difference.
perf.currentCost: Two identical method bodies; the 'tmp' parameter in Run is never used, so Run and RunNaive are functionally indistinguishable. Larger compiled code, more icache pressure, maintenance hazard.
perf.proposedChange: Either implement the Brent-Kung baby-step/giant-step composition in Run (O(n^2 / sqrt or n sqrt(n) log) with the tmp scratch it was given) so the two methods genuinely differ, or delete RunNaive and keep one. As-is, collapse to one method.
perf.rationale: Removes duplicated code path; if the intended design was a fast Run vs naive fallback, the tmp parameter signals an unfinished Brent-Kung implementation that would lower composition from O(n^2*m) toward O(n^1.5 log n).
perf.risk: Pure ergonomics/dedup unless the faster algorithm is implemented; deleting RunNaive is an API change for callers. State clearly which to keep. No semantic change from dedup since bodies are identical.
